summary: This repository is a Terraform Splunk Observability demo: collector agents, a gateway, optional Astronomy Shop, and one in-repo Python Lambda handler.
The Lambda already bootstraps Splunk APM traces through AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER=/opt/otel-instrument, but OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES only sets a non-semconv environment= alias.
The handler reads ApproximateNumberOfMessages and writes SQS/DynamoDB outcomes with print(); it emits no app-owned queue-depth or consume/put metrics.
Host collectors and the gateway already export traces and metrics to Splunk Observability; nginx/apache/mysql metrics rely on collector discovery plus hostmetrics.
Astronomy Shop including product-reviews and llm is deployed from container images. GenAI spans, tokens, and workflow names are owned by those images, not this repo's application source.
Highest-priority app-owned work is Lambda resource identity, then SQS/DynamoDB worker metrics. Select those findings and run $otel-instrument.
flow: audit -> select -> instrument -> verify -> configure/dashboard -> publish

findings.title: Lambda resource attributes omit deployment.environment.name
findings.gap: The Lambda sets OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=lambda_sqs_dynamodb and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=environment=${var.environment}. Source does not set deployment.environment.name, service.version, or any other semantic resource identity besides the custom environment alias.
findings.impact: Operators cannot break down Lambda traces and metrics by the OpenTelemetry environment dimension used on collector and Astronomy Shop resources.
findings.product_outcome: Operators should see lambda_sqs_dynamodb in APM filtered by deployment.environment.name matching the Terraform environment, with the existing environment alias still present for current dashboards.
findings.required_fix: Add deployment.environment.name=${var.environment} to OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES while preserving the existing environment alias and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=lambda_sqs_dynamodb. Do not hard-code service.name in a way that overwrites the operator OTEL_SERVICE_NAME.
acceptance_criteria: The existing environment=${var.environment} alias is preserved.
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME remains lambda_sqs_dynamodb and is not overwritten by resource attributes.
constraints: Preserve the existing environment resource alias; adding deployment.environment.name is additive.
Do not put user, queue message id, or request id on resource attributes.

follow_up_actions: After instrumentation, confirm lambda_sqs_dynamodb appears in Splunk Observability Studio with deployment.environment.name matching the Terraform environment.

findings.title: Lambda SQS and DynamoDB worker lacks detector-ready outcome metrics
findings.gap: lambda_handler reads ApproximateNumberOfMessages and performs SQS receive, DynamoDB put_item, and SQS delete, but only print()s those outcomes. There is no Meter, no messaging.destination.depth, no consume/put count or duration metric, and no recordException on the handler path. Wrapper AWS SDK spans may exist but are not detector-ready queue-depth or outcome metrics.
findings.impact: A growing SQS backlog or DynamoDB put failure is not chartable or alertable without searching traces or CloudWatch logs.
findings.product_outcome: Operators should see a queue-depth chart, SQS consume rate/errors, and DynamoDB put latency/errors for lambda_sqs_dynamodb without opening individual traces.
findings.required_fix: From lambda_handler, emit a low-cardinality messaging.destination.depth gauge from ApproximateNumberOfMessages, messaging.client.consumed.messages on successful receive/delete, and db.client.operation.duration for put_item with error.type on failure. Record span exception/status on handler failures. Do not add message body, MessageId, or raw payload as metric attributes.
acceptance_criteria: A successful consume path emits messaging.destination.depth from ApproximateNumberOfMessages with only queue and operation dimensions.
A successful put_item emits db.client.operation.duration with db.system=aws.dynamodb and no message body attributes.
A forced receive or put failure sets span status ERROR and a low-cardinality error.type, and increments an error outcome on the matching metric.
Existing stdout print() behavior remains so CloudWatch operators keep the current sink.
constraints: Do not use MessageId, message body, or user-generated text as metric attributes.
Keep print() stdout; do not replace CloudWatch logging with an OTLP log exporter on this traces-only Lambda.
Prefer OpenTelemetry messaging and db semantic names over custom aliases.

expected_telemetry.product_view: SQS backlog chart and detector for lambda_sqs_dynamodb

expected_telemetry.product_view: SQS consume rate and error chart

expected_telemetry.product_view: DynamoDB put latency and error chart

follow_up_actions: After instrumentation, chart messaging.destination.depth and DynamoDB put errors in Splunk Observability Studio before adding detectors.

environments.prerequisites: No live AWS credentials. Use moto or in-memory fakes for SQS and DynamoDB. Runtime is Python 3.9 as configured on the function.
No cloud apply. Inspect the environment.variables map in source.

scenarios.expected_signals: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES contains deployment.environment.name and the preserved environment alias; OTEL_SERVICE_NAME is lambda_sqs_dynamodb
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Source shows deployment.environment.name=${var.environment} plus environment=${var.environment} and does not overwrite service.name

scenarios.expected_signals: handler or consume span status ERROR, error.type, and messaging.client.consumed.messages error datapoint
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Failure records span exception/status and an error outcome without MessageId or body attributes

scenarios.trigger: Invoke lambda_handler with a fake DynamoDB table that accepts put_item
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: One duration datapoint for put_item without payload or MessageId dimensions

anti_patterns: Lambda OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES uses a custom environment key instead of deployment.environment.name.
lambda_handler uses print() for operational SQS depth and DynamoDB outcomes instead of instruments.

Phone Shop still installs the legacy SignalFx agent and SIGNALFX_* tracing URLs rather than OpenTelemetry packages; that module is marked unsupported in README.md and its Lambda source is downloaded at apply time.
product-reviews sets OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true, which captures prompt/response content in a demo.
recommendation: Select OTEL-001 and optionally OTEL-002 in the report, copy the generated prompt, and run $otel-instrument.
